summary: Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) studied under Bruno Petzold. He held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University from circa 1961 to 1980 and at Asia University from circa 1980 to 1988.
Seijun Ishii (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 1981. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University circa 2004.

Seijun Sato (1932–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He held positions at Taisho University from circa 1978 to 2003 and at Ishigami Zen'nō Kyōju Koki Kinen Ronbunshū Kankōkai around 2001.

Buddhist studies scholar Seikaku Hirata (1924–2008) studied at Kyoto University (circa 1946–1949) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from circa 1955 to 1994.

Sein Tin (1899–1942) worked in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon (circa 1918–1921), and Christ Church, Oxford (circa 1921–1923), studying under Pe Maung Tin from 1924 to 1927.

Seiran Ouchi (1845–1918) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Nishi Hongan-ji and served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918, having founded Hoshi Sodan in 1874 and Meikyo Shinshi in 1875.

Seiren Matsunami (1912–1989), a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1965, 1979), Rissho University (attested 1972), and Taisho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima (1957–2019) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including von Hinüber, Ji, and Norman, later holding professorships at the IRIAB at Soka University (1998–2019).

Seishin Kato (1872–1956), a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University, Taisho University, and Toyo University, and taught at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University.
Seitatsu Matsunami is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held positions as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1992.

Seizan Yanagida (1922–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto Universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, later holding professorships at Hanazono University, Kyoto University (1976–1986), and Chubu University (circa 1996–2003).

Semen Ivanovich Tyulyaev (1898–1993) studied at Moscow State University. Specializing in art history, archaeology, and Indology, he worked at the State Museum of Oriental Art (1927–1958), the State Institute for Art Studies (circa 1944–1988), and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1958–1961).

Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1977 and between 1990 and 1998.

Semën Gesselevič Rudin (1929–1973) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his undergraduate and candidate degrees at Saint Petersburg State University (1947–1952, degree by 1968), where he also held an academic post beginning in 1955.

Sen Wang (1912–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University from circa 1932 to 1936 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1952 to 1980.

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Senarath Paranavitana (1896–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean Philippe Vogel and held a post at Leiden University from circa 1936 to 1937.

Senchu Murano (born 1908) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (circa 1930–1933) and the University of Washington (circa 1935–1938). He served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1959 to 1978.

Sengaku Mayeda (1931–2026), an Indologist and philosopher, studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Hajime Nakamura. He taught at Pennsylvania, Tokyo (1973, 1982–1991), and Musashino University (circa 1991–2001).

Senkyo Sakawa (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985; later professor emeritus) and was affiliated with the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.
